visual_events.label: Adjusting top brick on edge at wall corner
visual_events.description: In a medium-close high-angle static shot of a red brick wall corner built with bricks on edge and hollow internal cavities, a mason on the right (ent_mason) bends over and uses his left hand to press and adjust a newly laid brick on edge along the right-hand course while his right hand holds a long wooden straightedge (ent_straightedge) low against the wall face. In the upper-left background, the legs of a second person (ent_bystander) stand stationary near two stacked piles of bricks and an L-shaped metal square (ent_framing_square) on the dirt ground.
visual_events.context_result: The top course of bricks on edge sits in place with visible hollow cavities between the inner and outer wythes.

visual_events.label: Checking brick face alignment with wooden straightedge
visual_events.description: The mason (ent_mason) lifts the long wooden straightedge (ent_straightedge) with both hands from the lower right (approx. 1.2s–2.5s), positions it horizontally flush against the outer right-hand face of the top course of bricks on edge (approx. 2.5s–3.5s), and holds it against the bricks while pressing and nudging the top brick inward with his right hand to align it with the straightedge (approx. 3.5s–6.5s). Around 6.5s–6.8s he begins lifting the straightedge away from the wall face.
visual_events.context_result: The outer faces of the top-course bricks on edge are aligned flush along the straightedge line.

background_knowledge: In masonry practice, pressing a straight wooden rule or batten across freshly laid bricks on a mortar bed aligns their outer faces into a single plane before the mortar sets.
